finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts::vim `u` / `<c-r>` undo depends on an unverified assumption about `@replit/codemirror-vim`; if wrong, vim users lose undo entirely and silently
evidence: The claim hinges on `@replit/codemirror-vim` capturing `CodeMirror.commands.undo` when the vim action is defined rather than at call time. That is not what the package does: it is a port of CM5's `vim.js`, whose `actions.undo`/`actions.redo` bodies read `CodeMirror.commands.undo`/`.redo` inside the function (`repeatFn(cm, CodeMirror.commands.undo, ...)`), so the reassignment in `editor.ts:57-58` is live and vim `u` / `<C-r>` do reach `store.undo()/redo()`. The secondary claim that `defaultVimHistory` (editor.ts:38-41) could snapshot `undefined` and throw is also wrong — the adapter populates `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` during its own module init, which runs on the `import { CodeMirror, vim }` at editor.ts:5. What is genuinely true is only that no test presses `u` in vim mode (editor.test.ts covers Ctrl-z in default mode and the read-only mount), which is a coverage gap rather than a defect in the code as written; I could not inspect the pinned package source in this environment, hence medium confidence.
